$comment: The Luz design tokens, in one place and in no platform's language (ADR-0031, DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3).
tooling/scripts/generate_design_tokens.py turns this into the Android token file; the Apple apps read the same
values when they arrive (Phase 11-12), so the two platforms cannot drift apart by hand-editing one of them.
Colours are sRGB hex. Sizes are density-independent (dp/pt) and text sizes scale with the platform's text setting.

color.$comment: A near-black blue-charcoal environment rather than flat black, a soft-white text ramp, and the Luz amber used sparingly: progress, the selected mark, the one action a screen wants. Layers differ by a few percent of luminance — enough to read as depth, never enough to read as grey boxes.

bgBase.$comment: Not #000000: the owner's directive asks for a deep, faintly blue charcoal so the screen reads as a space rather than a hole. Every gradient over artwork ends in this colour, so pictures dissolve into the room instead of into a black edge.

bgSurface1.use: the first layer above the environment: a list, a pane

lineSubtle.use: hairlines and the track behind a progress bar

textPrimary.use: titles and anything that must be read at 3 m — a soft white, not a glaring one

accent.use: primary actions, selection, focus ring, progress
accent.$comment: Sampled from the owner's logo (hue 28, the mark's core amber) and lightened until it reads on #0B0D10: 9.4:1 against the base, and near-black text on it passes comfortably.

accentPressed.use: the accent while a control is being pressed

onAccent.use: text and icons drawn on top of the accent

stateLive.use: the live marker and the now-line in the guide

stateOk.use: working: a connected provider, a loaded guide — a small dot, never a fill

focusRing.use: the hairline around a focused card, under the lift
focusRing.$comment: White at low opacity, not amber. The owner chose the Apple TV app as the reference: there, focus is a lift — scale, a soft shadow, a brighter surface — and colour stays in the artwork. The amber is still the app's accent: progress, selection, the primary action.

scrimTop.use: the transparent end of a gradient laid over artwork

scrimBottom.use: the solid end of that gradient, the environment colour

material.$comment: Surfaces are not grey paint: they are white or dark laid over what is behind them, at an opacity, with a hairline of white to catch the edge. That is how the reference app gets depth without drawing boxes. Where the reference blurs, this hardware cannot, so materials that sit over busy content are denser.

panel.use: a menu, a sheet, the navigation panel: dark, lifting off what is behind it

raised.use: a resting control or row: white laid on very faintly

raisedFocused.use: the same surface under the remote

hairline.use: the one-pixel edge that separates a surface from what is behind it

scrim.use: what dims the screen behind a modal

text.$comment: Roles, not fonts: each platform uses its own system typeface. The scale follows tvOS proportions — its points are drawn on a 1920x1080 canvas, and a 1080p Android television renders 960x540 dp, so a tvOS size halves into sp here. Tracking tightens as size grows.

display.use: a screen's own title, the search field

headline.use: a detail page's title when there is no hero, a settings section

subtitle.use: buttons, a list row's name, a card title that needs weight

body.use: descriptions — the smallest size for anything read as a sentence

callout.use: card titles, the metadata line under a hero

caption.use: the line under a card title, counts, times

space.$comment: A 4-point scale; names are the multiplier (space4 = 16). Named sizes in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md map onto it: XS=space1, S=space2, M=space4, L=space6, XL=space10, XXL=space16.

safeHorizontal.use: TV overscan margin, left and right

safeVertical.use: TV overscan margin, top and bottom

radius.$comment: Soft, not bubbly. The reference app's artwork corners are small; only buttons go fully round.

motion.$comment: Fast, smooth, quiet: ease-out curves, no springs, nothing that bounces. Focus answers the remote instantly; scenery (the hero, the ambient colour) changes slowly so it never competes with the remote.

focus.$comment: Focus has physical presence: the item comes towards the viewer — a little larger, on a soft shadow, a shade brighter. The hairline is a whisper under that, not an outline.

layout.$comment: Sizes of the shared pieces, for a 960x540 dp television. Fractions are of the screen height.

heroHeightFraction.use: how much of the screen a hero takes; the first shelf peeks in below

landscapeWidth.use: a 16:9 card: continue watching, an episode, a channel

railCollapsedWidth.use: the navigation at rest: icons only

railExpandedWidth.use: the navigation under the remote: icons and names

contentStart.use: where content begins, clear of the resting navigation

shelfSpacing.use: the space between one shelf and the next

cardGap.use: the space between cards on a shelf
